page: Alibaba Cloud ecs.e-c1m2.xlarge is an entry-tier shared compute instance based on the x86_64 architecture. Driven by an Intel Xeon processor running at a base clock speed of 2.5 GHz, the instance provides 4 shared vCPUs mapped to 2 physical cores across 2 threads per core. Memory capacity is configured at 8.0 GB of RAM, establishing a 1:2 vCPU-to-memory ratio with 2.0 GB per vCPU. The host CPU architecture supports AVX, AVX-512F, AES, and FMA instruction extensions, backed by 32 KB L1d cache, 1.0 MB L2 cache, and a 33 MB shared L3 cache. There are no onboard GPUs or local storage devices bundled with the configuration, requiring attached network block storage for persistence.

In benchmark testing, the shared CPU allocation yields modest throughput across synthetic and application-level workloads. On stress-ng, the instance records 1199.89 points in single-core and 3141.11 points in multi-core tests, placing in the lower quartile. Geekbench scores reflect shared resource limits, attaining 716.0 for single-core and 657.0 for multi-core processing, alongside a clang compilation mark of 553.0. Compression tests demonstrate 21.49 GB/sec on single-threaded gzip, while multi-threaded bzip3 decompression reaches 8.45 GB/sec. Data and memory tasks registered 1.19 million operations per second on Redis SET and 0.24 GB/sec in static web serving throughput, reflecting baseline network bandwidth of 0 Gbps.

The ecs.e-c1m2.xlarge offers an economical footprint within the cloud provider shared fleet by trading dedicated core performance for budget efficiency. Because CPU time is shared and baseline network bandwidth is constrained, performance fluctuates under sustained concurrent pressure, as indicated by multi-core Geekbench metrics. Consequently, this server profile is best suited for non-production environments, dev/test instances, lightweight internal tools, simple microservices, and low-traffic staging servers that do not demand sustained compute power or high disk throughput.
